sentences.text: The dinosaur likely possessed a relatively deep snout, a trait indicated by the square shape of its premaxilla bone.
Its nostrils were positioned near the tip of the snout, while a large, circular eye socket resembled that of the early dinosaur Eoraptor.
Four teeth lined each side of the premaxilla bone.
Two bony shelves extended from the inner surface of the premaxilla, stacking one above the other.
These stacked shelves serve as unique features that distinguish this genus from related sauropodomorphs.
The nasal bone was plate-like and featured four bony extensions: two pointing forward and two pointing backward.
Unlike the triangular shape seen in most related genera, the lower forward process of this bone was tongue-shaped and wider than the upper one.
The postorbital bone formed the upper rear corner of the eye socket and bore three large processes extending forward, downward, and backward.
A fourth small process on this bone pointed upward and inward to connect with the parietal bone, an orientation unique among dinosaurs.
The rear-projecting process of the postorbital bone ended in a bifurcated tip rather than tapering, unlike most other basal sauropodomorphs.
The discovery of two right nasal bones suggests that at least two individuals lived at the fossil site.
Evidence such as small size and open bone sutures indicates these fossils likely represent juveniles.
Adam Yates, Matthew Bonnan, and Johann Neveling first named the dinosaur Arcusaurus in 2011.
The genus name derives from the Latin word for 'rainbow', referencing the Rainbow Nation.
The species name honors Lucille Pereira and Fernando Abdala, who discovered the fossils.
Fossils were collected in March 2006 from the Spion Kop Heelbo site in Senekal, Free State, South Africa.
The holotype specimen, which is the specimen the species is based on, is a partial skull with the catalog number BP/1/6235.
Detailed analysis confirmed that the fossils were not juveniles of the species Aardonyx or Massospondylus.
The close relationship between Arcusaurus and the Late Triassic dinosaur Efraasia implies a 35-million-year ghost lineage for sauropodomorphs.
Phylogenetic studies classify Arcusaurus as a basal sauropodomorph, sister to Efraasia and more derived sauropodomorphs.
It is classified within the order Saurischia and the suborder Sauropodomorpha.
Arcusaurus lived in South Africa during the Early Jurassic period, specifically the Pliensbachian stage.
The time range for this animal is estimated to be between 201.4 and 192.9 million years ago.
It is debated whether Arcusaurus belongs with basal sauropodomorphs, as it possesses unique features of the advanced clade Plateosauria that raise doubts about phylogenetic results.
